column3: “valiant warrior” renders “mighty man of strength”; “harlot” renders “prostitute,” and “Gilead was the father of Jephthah” renders “Gilead fathered Jephthah.”
“when you are in trouble” renders “when distress is yours.”
NASB renders the last clause as a question, “will I become your head?”; the Hebrew reads as a statement, “I will become your head.”
“is witness” renders “will be hearing”; “surely” renders the oath form “if not.”
“What is between you and me” renders “What is to me and to you.”
“they said” is plural for the Hebrew singular “he said.”
“the Red Sea” renders “the Sea of Reeds.”
“let us pass” renders “let me pass”; “consent” renders “be willing.”
“the east side” renders “the rising of the sun.”
“let us pass … to our place” renders “let me pass … to my place.”
“any better” renders the doubled “really good”; “ever strive” renders the doubled verb.
“disregarded the message” renders “did not listen to the words.”
NASB supplies “so that” and “went on to.”
